name: Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation Type 4
aliases: Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation Type IV

criteria.description: Presence of large peripheral cystic lesions in the lung on imaging
Histopathological confirmation showing cysts lined by alveolar type epithelium with thin fibrous septa
No evidence of other congenital lung malformations such as bronchopulmonary sequestration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lung lesions on imaging plus histopathological confirmation of type 4 CPAM
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal ultrasound and postnatal CT imaging are critical for diagnosis; histopathology confirms subtype.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically unilateral and located in the peripheral lung
Often presents shortly after birth due to mass effect

common.notes: Due to cystic spaces predisposing to infection
Increased respiratory rate due to compromised lung function

common.symptomName: Decreased breath sounds over affected lung
common.notes: Due to cystic lesions occupying lung parenchyma
searchTerms: reduced breath sounds over lung area

occasional.notes: Shift of mediastinal structures due to large cystic mass
Underdevelopment of lung tissue adjacent to cysts
Fluid accumulation secondary to cyst rupture or infection

rare.notes: Due to rupture of cystic lesions

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible leukocytosis if infected
imaging: Chest X-ray showing large cystic lesions
CT scan demonstrating peripheral large cysts with thin walls
Prenatal ultrasound showing cystic lung mass
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology showing cysts lined by alveolar type epithelium with thin fibrous septa

distinguishingFeatures: Different histopathology lacking alveolar epithelium lining
Overinflation of a pulmonary lobe without cystic lesions
No discrete cystic masses on imaging
Histology shows alveolar overdistension rather than cyst formation

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress requiring ventilation
Rapidly enlarging cystic lung mass causing mediastinal shift
references: Stocker JT. Congenital pulmonary airway malformation: a new name for and an expanded classification of congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung. Histopathology. 2002.
Langston C. New concepts in the pathology of congenital lung malformations. Semin Pediatr Surg. 2003.
Orphanet: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 4 (ORPHA:280854)
